newsitem.title: UK: Sidlaw sells oil services for 56 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: Sidlaw sells oil services for 56 mln stg.

text.p: Sidlaw Group Plc said it had entered into conditional agreement to sell its oil services division for 56 million stg, allowing it to become a focused flexible packaging business.
It said after the sale, it would be ungeared with a small cash balance.
Sidlaw said the buyer would be Secretside, a new company set up to buy the oil services unit, with the backing of 3i Group and Clydesdale Bank.
Sidlaw said this would provide it with "a sound financial base for investing in the future," adding that it should see a pretax gain on the sale of around 17 million stg.

Sidlaw added that in the first two months of the last quarter of its financial year, the oil services unit performed above the level of a year earlier while in flexible packaging, recovery was slow but in line with expectations.
It said raw materials costs remained relatively stable but there was still pressure on pricing from customers.
Sidlaw's shares gained 15p to 125p by 0900 GMT after it announced the oil services unit sale.
Sidlaw said its key objective in packaging would be "to improve operating margins and thereby enhance shareholder returns."
Initially it would focus on developing the core European flexible packaging business which accounts for some 70 percent of the division's turnover.
Sidlaw intended "to adopt a more conservative approach to gearing commensurate with the operational requirements of the packaging business."
But the group said it did not believe a distribution to shareholders from the proceeds of the disposal would be in the interests of the ongoing business at this time.
